BACKGROUND (design review Step 4, 'opt-in disclosure guards'). Today a world entity's name and aliases are all compiled by storygame/story_package/loader.py _compile_knowledge_indexes into indexes.entity_alias_to_entities, and storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py (_validate_segments, first loop) rejects narration that uses such a phrase when no owner of it is nameable (code narration_known_term_leak). So declaring an ordinary object changes which words are accepted in other scenes, and a secret has no way to say 'guard this term until THIS fact is true'. Scoped aliases (Entity.scoped_aliases, resolver ItemFactsProvider._resolve_scoped_entity in storygame/runtime/item_facts.py) already name an entity only while it is placed and in scene scope and never enter the guard index.

TASK T1: explicit disclosure policy and guards, with the legacy path kept as the default.
OWNED FILES (edit nothing else): storygame/story_package/models.py, storygame/story_package/loader.py, storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py, tests/test_disclosure_guards.py (new), docs/markdown-story-authoring.md (one short subsection). Notes path: /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/design-review-step4-notes/t1.md

DESIGN (follow exactly):
1. models.py: add `disclosure: Literal['legacy','public'] = 'legacy'` on Entity. 'legacy' = today's behaviour for every existing declaration (no story data changes in this task). 'public' = the entity's name and aliases are ordinary words: they are NOT added to indexes.entity_alias_to_entities for that entity (if another non-public entity shares a form, that other entity still indexes it). Scoped aliases keep working as today. Add to WorldSource `disclosure_guards: tuple[DisclosureGuard, ...] = ()` where DisclosureGuard is a frozen model: `id` (pattern _ID), `terms: tuple[str, ...]` (min 1, each non-blank), `audience: Literal['player'] = 'player'` (reserved for later audiences), `unlock_fact: str | None`, `unlock_knowledge_id: str | None` (exactly one of the two must be set). Add to KnowledgeIndexes `disclosure_guards: Mapping[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}` mapping each lookup form (use term_lookup_forms, as the other loops do) to guard ids.
2. loader.py: compile the guard index in _compile_knowledge_indexes. Validate at load (raise StoryPackageError with a message naming the guard or entity id): unlock_fact must be in world.facts; unlock_knowledge_id must be a knowledge id in the catalog; guard ids unique; no guard term may equal (after term_lookup_forms normalisation) the name, alias or scoped alias of a disclosure='public' entity; a hidden item (Item.hidden true) or an entity with named_by set must not be disclosure='public' (a secret needs a guard, not a public name). Find where other package validation lives (e.g. _validate_knowledge or the world validation that checks scoped aliases near line 1098) and put the checks beside it.
3. narration_safety.py: add one new loop in _validate_segments, after the protected_terms loop. For each guard form found in the segment text (self._contains), skip when the guard is unlocked in the CANDIDATE state (unlock_fact asserted true in candidate_state.facts, using the same truth test as true_fact_ids; or unlock_knowledge_id in earned_ids), or when handoff_text contains the form (same exemption the other loops give), otherwise raise ProposalValidationError(f"narration mentions guarded term '{form}'", code='disclosure_guard_leak'). The guard is global: it does NOT depend on scene scope or on the term's entity being nameable. Do not change the three existing loops' behaviour for legacy records.
4. docs/markdown-story-authoring.md: a short 'Disclosure policy' subsection next to the scoped_aliases sentence: absent = legacy; public = ordinary word; secrets get a disclosure_guards entry with terms and an unlock fact or knowledge id; a new declaration should pick one on purpose.

TESTS (tests/test_disclosure_guards.py, build packages by loading the real continuity-initiative package and then using pydantic model_copy / dataclass replace on world.items and world.disclosure_guards, as other tests such as tests/test_scoped_aliases.py do; follow that file's helpers): (a) a public item named with a plain-word alias is accepted in narration in a scene where it is not placed, while the same item left legacy is rejected there (narration_known_term_leak); (b) adding a public item changes no verdict for a fixed list of >=8 unrelated sentences across >=3 scenes (compare accept/reject and code against the unmodified package); (c) a guard with unlock_fact rejects its term with code disclosure_guard_leak before the fact and accepts it after the fact is asserted, in a scene where the term's entity would otherwise be nameable (global, not scene-scoped); (d) unlock_knowledge_id variant; (e) each loader validation error above fires with a message naming the id; (f) a guard term already covered by the handoff text of a staged handoff is accepted; (g) the real, unmodified package still loads and every existing test passes (legacy default). Player input strings are imperative commands in the player's voice, never 'Wait.'.

TASK T2: make recall and the resolver agree on scoped aliases.
OWNED FILES (edit nothing else): storygame/runtime/knowledge.py, storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, tests/test_scoped_alias_recall.py (new). Notes path: /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/design-review-step4-notes/t2.md
